utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, the witness can be escorted in the courtroom. Meanwhile, I use the time. First of all, to briefly revisit the matter of the updated 65 ter summary of the witness which we discussed yesterday. Mr. Mladic, no greeting to the public gallery. We missed the updated 65 ter summary which was sent on the 25th of March. We have taken proper care that it will not happen again. We received that information only the day before yesterday very late in the evening. I mean, we, the Judges. We'll take care that it doesn't happen again. At the same time, all observations we made about just changing a 65 ter document, whether that's an exhibit list, whether that's a witness list or whether that is a 65 ter summary of the expected testimony of the witness of course is subject to approval. That's the procedure followed is not the right one but we missed it, and we thought that it would be wise to put that on the record. Then, I have still a few other matters. The first one is one of the remaining issues of the testimony of Goran Krcmar, D917. On the 26th of February, 2015, D917, a video was marked for identification pending a selection of the sequences by the Defence. On the 25th of March, the Chamber set the deadline of the 1st of April for the Defence to make such selections. This can be found at transcript page 33693, but as of today, the Chamber has not heard from the Defence. Is there -- could the Defence please update the Chamber on the selection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know the full details but my understanding there are quite a number of selections and we're having some technical difficulties in terms of having to cut those excerpts from the master recording, as it were, to make a compilation of excerpts in compliance with Your Honours' instructions. We're working on that and we hope to get that done as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, since you are two weeks over the deadline, deadlines are to be contain seriously, we would like to know when you would expect to provide that selection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jeremic. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Ms. Hasan will now continue her cross-examination and would you please, when you answer any question, stay close to the microphone. Ms. Hasan, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours. Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Jeremic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we call up 043 --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we display 04315, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm just calling up the same document we were looking at yesterday and that's the statement of Nesko Djokic. And if I can ask that we take a look at page 2 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S. Do you recognise the signature on the right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Bogdanovic's.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 04315 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7302, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7302 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we now take a look at 65 ter 25698, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This, can you see, is dated the 26th of July, 1995. It's another statement. This time, a statement of Slobodan Djokic, son of Nesko, born 1 December 1975 [sic] in D. Likanj, Zvornik municipality. 1971 is the year of birth. Mr. Jeremic, you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it's recorded here that Slobodan Djokic is from D. Likanj, Zvornik municipality, would that be an inaccurate recollection of where he is from, which is Lokanj?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Lokanj.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And again, this is a statement regarding the assistance that was provided to the enemy as is stated there. Now, if we turn to page 3 in the B/C/S and page 2 in the English, please, again, there's a signature there. Do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Goran Bogdanovic's.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And Slobodan Djokic, that would have been the son of Nesko Djokic; correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you were present, am I right, when he was interviewed?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 25698 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7303, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7303 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You mentioned briefly yesterday that the Muslim men who were brought to the Standard Barracks were -- had some bruises and injuries on their faces. This is at transcript page 34305, lines 23 to 24. Besides the bruises and injuries you've told us about, how did they appear to you when they were first brought in?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I said yesterday that they had injuries and bruises on their faces. As a matter of fact, I said that they did not have any bruises or injuries on their faces.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we have your clarification then on the record. So then let's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Ms. Hasan, you read the relevant lines to the witness. And if the witness still claims that that is not what he said, then we would verify that on the basis of the audio. Witness, whatever you said, we have an opportunity to verify it on the basis of the audio recording of yesterday's hearing, so Ms. Hasan will now read to you what you are recorded to have said and if you still disagree then we'll have an opportunity to verify that, including the translation given.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So I'll start reading your answer beginning on line 21: "I don't remember that their clothes were covered with blood but I remember that their clothes were torn and not in a good state of repair. But I do remember that they had some bruises and injuries on their faces." So, Witness, does that reflect what you told us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember having said that. Give me the original. Give me my original statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, this is what you were recorded to have said yesterday. We have the English translation available, but that might not assist you that much. We have an opportunity to verify or to have verified what you said on the basis of the audio, and then verify whether the translation that was given to us was an accurate translation, yes or no. If you say, That's not what I said, we'll have it verified, but I can't give you at this moment any B/C/S version of this is what you said yesterday in this courtroom yesterday as it was recorded. You still challenge that that's what you said or would you consider that this is possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I challenge that. It is not possible that I said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have it verified.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So, Mr. Jeremic, could you then tell us how did they appear to you, these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all right, of course, they looked frightened, and their clothes were dirty, torn, dishevelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we now take a look at 65 ter 04360.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So we see here it's dated 23rd of July, 1995. It's a statement of Emin Mustafic, son of Rifet, there's some biographical information there, born in 1969 in Drinjaca, member of the 280th Eastern Bosnian Light Brigade. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Is that your signature on the right at the end of that statement under your name?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 04360 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7304, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we now see 65 ter 04362, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, this is dated 23 July 1995. It's a statement of Almir Halilovic, son of Suljo, born 25 August 1980 in the village of Bajramovici. And if we turn to page 2 in the English, 3 in the B/C/S, on the right-hand side there under your name, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Mr. Jeremic, I know you've seen these documents numerous times in the past. If you need the opportunity to review it a little bit more, please let me know. Otherwise I'll ask you to tell me whether you recognise this as the statement you took from Almir Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, if we go back to the first page in the English and we just stay with page 3 in the B/C/S, about halfway down the page, after describing how they were following Nesko and his son's instructions on how to get to -- how to cross the front lines, they were exhausted, got lost, and then surrendered in a Serb village. And it records here: "We surrendered" --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Actually, could I ask ... could I ask to go to page 2 in the English. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So it says --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can I just see the full page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: "We had reason to believe" - this is where they surrendered - "that it was a Serbian village and we surrendered there to a man called Bojo. He also gave us food and cigarettes and then took us to the VRS command. "All four of us were taken from there to Ugljevik where we were interrogated. After that, we were escorted by the police to detention in the army barracks in Zvornik." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And isn't it the case that Drago Nikolic had told you that the military police would be bringing in four persons of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember now whether he said that the military police would bring them in, but he told me down there when we were at the office that somebody would come. Now, did he say four persons of Muslim ethnicity? Well, anyway two Serb soldiers who helped on his assumption helped Muslim soldiers, civilians and that a statement should be taken from the Serb soldiers and from the Muslims who had been taken prisoner so that later Nesko and his son, Slobodan, would be punished because they helped the enemy. That's what he said to me. But who would bring them, I do not remember that he told me who it was that would bring them in. And later on, they did come. Soon later.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let me see if I can help you remember. Do you recall testifying in the Trbic case before the State Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina? This is in December of 2007.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, did you tell the truth when you provided your testimony to that court?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I was telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter 32420.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, this is a transcript, what will appear as a transcript of your testimony in that case. I'd ask for page 14 to be displayed, and it's in English, it's been transcribed from the audio, the B/C/S audio, so I'm going to read it out to you. At line 7, you were asked about what Drago Nikolic had told you. And you respond: "He told me that the military police would bring in four persons of Muslim ethnicity, I believe -- And then if we skip down to line 13, you say: "He came into my office because it was on the ground floor, and he told me that military police would bring in four persons of Muslim ethnicity, that according to his information and indications he believed that those four persons were guarded by Serbs on the front line," and so on and so forth. Now, Witness, do you stand by the testimony that you gave to that court?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I think the last statement we were looking at, that of Almir Halilovic, I'd offer that into evidence; 65 ter 04362, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7305, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next statement, 65 ter 04359.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Another statement. It's dated 23 July 1995. We see it's a statement of Sakib Kiviric, son of Salko, born 24 June 1964 in Jagodinja municipality of Bratunac, member of the 283rd Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade. Now I'm going to ask to keep that name of the village Jagodinja in mind because I'm going to come back to that. If we turn to page 2 in the English and 3 in the B/C/S, can you tell us again whether you recognise the signature on the right as yours?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the signature, and yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you confirm this is the statement you took from Sakib Kiviric?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 04359 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7306, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Finally, 65 ter 04360?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that not P7304 already, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You're right, I misspoke. 04361, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: All right. So now we have a statement dated the 26th of July, 1995. It's from Fuad Dzozic, son of father Senusija born 2 May, 1965 in Zegojno, Srebrenica municipality, member of the 280th Mountain Brigade. Now, if we turn to page 2 in the English, 3 in the B/C/S, please, and I'll ask you if you recognise the signature on the right-hand side there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Whose signature is it?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cedo Jovic's.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And having -- if we turn back to the first page is of this statement could you confirm that this was in fact the statement taken from the fourth prisoner, Fuad Dzozic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 04361 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7307, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, sir, these Muslim prisoners, they were made to identify the father and the son who aided them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You were present during that identification process?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we please display 65 ter 04363, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is dated the 25th of July, 1995. It's a record. And it reads -- as record of the identification of Nesko Djokic and Slobodan Djokic. And if we just skip a few lines. "The identification procedure was carried out by Goran Bogdanovic, an authorised official of the military police. "The following were present during the identification ..." And it lists Lieutenant Drago Nikolic, chief of security. Goran Bogdanovic, officer of the crime prevention department. And Nebojsa Jeremic, officer of the crime prevention department. Now is that consistent with your recollection as to who was present during this identification procedure?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if this is in the document and if this is how it is in the document, then I suppose it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's go to page 2, please. In the B/C/S as well, please. Do you recognise that signature as belonging to Goran Bogdanovic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And let's turn back a page just after it lists who was present during the identification procedure, we see the names of the four Muslim prisoners. Now, as far as you can recall, did the prisoners identify the Djokic father and son independently of each other?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember whether it was done individually. I don't know whether they saw them individually, first one and then the other. In any case, I remember that they recognised them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. We see just three-quarters of the way down the page, in the -- what appears to be the second-to-last paragraph, last line: "The enemy soldiers independently picked them out and identified them." Does that help you remember whether they identified them independently?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "each and every one of them independently," so if that's how it's written, then I suppose that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And just briefly, if I can go back again to page 2, because we see a stamp on the B/C/S document, do you recognise that stamp?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Military post. The military post of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 4356 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, I made a mistake. 65 ter 4363.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7308, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And now turning to 65 ter 04356, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is we're looking at here?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a ruling on detention or, rather, on remanding Nesko Djokic and his son, Slobodan, in custody for three days.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And we see here that it records that detention shall last - excuse me - from 24 July at 1200 hours to 27 July at 1200 hours. Now if we turn the page in the English and the B/C/S - page 3 in the B/C/S, please - do you recognise the signature there?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic's, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, again, that's the stamp of the Zvornik Brigade; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now I understand that you don't know who -- you don't recall who drafted this particular document. But can you confirm that the information provided therein about the detention is accurate?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 20 years ago. If it says that their detention lasted three days, then I suppose that the document is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd offer 65 ter 4356 into evidence. I think I have that number correct. 65 ter 4356. Your Honour, could we have that document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7309, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you testified that the father -- the Djokic father and son were sent somewhere, you thought to Han Pijesak, to prison or to the front line. This is at transcript page 34298, starting at line 8. And just so we're all clear and to avoid any confusion, can you explain the relationship as you understand it between the three-day detention that we just saw on this record before us and the 60-military imprisonment that was ordered by Commander Vinko Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the details, but I know for sure that they may have been kept in detention for three days, pending the order of the brigade commander to send them for imprisonment of 60 days. Because in the Zvornik Brigade there was only detention, and a soldier could be kept for not more than 15 days. And then the soldiers who were sentenced, i.e., who received either a 30- or 60-day imprisonment pursuant to the commander's order, they were sent somewhere outside of the Zvornik Brigade. I believe it was somewhere around Han Pijesak. I don't know whether they were in prison for 30 or 60 days or whether they were immediately sent to the front line up there. I really can't tell you now, not for a fact because we never received any feedback. In any case, the biggest punishment for them was the fact that they had to be absent from their homes for 60 days. That's my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, the three-day detention did not cancel out, then, the 60 days of imprisonment?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we turn to 65 ter 04317, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: This is a report on the -- collaboration with the enemy. It's dated 26 July 1995 from the security organ of the Zvornik Brigade to the Military Prosecutor in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we turn to page 2 in the English and 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you recognise that signature and stamp?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And do you recall this particular document?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this document at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we turn then back to page 1, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The report is on the Djokic father and son, and it relates to the information provided by them and the four Muslim prisoners that they aided. Now, it's sent to the Military Prosecutor in Bijeljina. Did you understand that there were criminal charges that were being laid against the Djokic brother -- father and son?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know, I believe that a criminal report was supposed to be drafted, and these are all enclosures to that criminal report. I don't know whether that criminal report was ever drafted or not. In any case, there was an order to issue a criminal report against the two Djokics.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Do you know besides -- leaving aside murder cases, would it have been customary for you to receive information back from the Military Prosecutor's office about the disposition of charges that your unit had referred to the Military Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any feedback. I believe that our department never received any official information from the Military Prosecutor about the disposition of charges against soldiers of -- of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when Vinko Pandurevic issues an order for the imprisonment for a term of 60 days, did he have to await approval from the Military Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: I'm talking about the department specifically. Vinko Pandurevic never personally told us, Issue an order on behalf of the brigade commander. It was always communicated to us by Drago Nikolic, chief of security. So we never received a direct order from Pandurevic about either a -- the 30-day imprisonment or the 60-day imprisonment.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: But returning to my question, did you have an understanding that approval had to be sought from the military courts before 60-day of military imprisonment was issued?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd offer 65 ter 4317 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7310, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremic, now, this Chamber has received evidence from a survivor who had escaped executions at the Branjevo military farm and that he escaped together with four other Muslim men. One of the other survivors he was with was from Jagodinja. This is the village Sakib Kiviric was from, as is recorded in the statement you took.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is evidence from RM255 that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, this witness had observed blood on the clothing of the prisoner, and while he tried to keep up with the prisoners who -- the four other prisoners -- sorry. The four other Muslim men who were with him he said they were younger than him and he couldn't keep up and he lost them along the way. So it's our position, the Prosecution's position, that the four Muslims who survived the executions at the Branjevo farm on 16th, 17th July and who were encountered by Witness RM255 were the four Muslim men that Nesko Djokic and his son encountered near their house in Lokanj on 18 July 1995. Sir, you would agree with me that the village of Lokanj is located very near to the Branjevo military farm near Pilica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I know where the village of Lokanj is. I also know where Branjevo is. But I was never there during the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: But you'd agree that these locations, the village of Lokanj is very near to where these massacres took place at the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. This is a very broadly put question. When the Prosecutor says "very close," what does she mean? Can you specify the meaning of the phrase "very close."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let me do as following. Can the parties agree on what that distance is?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: We can certainly meet and agree to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both the question was --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe we can. When I examined the witness, Your Honour, you'll remember we had -- we maintained the same position, and we agreed to agree and in -- in order to avoid asking the witnesses to define any distance. I believe that we can agree on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General guidance for the parties: If the locations are known, are identified with sufficient precision, don't ask witnesses about distances but, rather, take a map and look at those maps. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one digression, Your Honours. I believe I am familiar with the area. The village of Lokanj is an elongated village so I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you want to say that it's not certain that the location of the village could be identified with sufficient precision, then, of course, if that would be an obstacle to reaching agreement - and you said a minute ago that you expected that you could - then, of course, that would perhaps be a problem, but even if a village is 500 metres long, which is perhaps longer than usual, then you still can say that from the one end of the village to Branjevo farm, it's that distance; from the other end of the village, it would be this distance. I mean, let's not bother witnesses with what the parties -- which is not in dispute apparently and which is to be resolved by the parties themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, you did understand that the four Muslim men who were brought to the Standard Barracks, from whom statements were taken, had survived a mass execution at the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. This is the first time I hear it from you. I really don't know anything about that. I was never in Branjevo. I don't know where they came from. They provided their statements the way they did, and ... I don't know. I haven't a clue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, have you never heard about a larger number of Muslims being executed or have been killed at Branjevo farm? Never heard about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did hear about that, but only after the war and while following the work of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you said I don't know anything about that. That's clear. "This is the first time I hear it from you." So that wasn't the truth, because you heard about it after the war earlier, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I heard about that after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I would kindly ask the witness to remove his headphones for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you understand the English language, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I also have a request that this objection should be put forth by my learned friend who speaks English. I wouldn't be able to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, is there any translation issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The issue is with Your Honour's question, which misstates the evidence. At transcript page 19, line 12 to 14, the question relates to the four Muslim men being from that massacre, which the witness said, he's hearing about it for the first time. So Your Honours' question misplaces the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If that is the case, let me re-read it. Yes, that's -- really some ambiguity in it. Whether he heard for the first time those who escaped. That's fully admitted, Mr. Ivetic, that I put it in a way to the witness which is not fair to him, and I apologise for that. Let's resume.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, witness, I will get back to your knowledge of the mass -- I will get back to [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I will get back to what you knew about the massacres that were taking place shortly. But at this point now, after the investigation of this case involving the Djokic father and son, you noticed that the four Muslim prisoners were no longer there at the barracks; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them after that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can take look at 65 ter 25697.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremic, this is a statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor on the 12th of January, 2006. Do you recognise your signature on the front page of that statement?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. And if we turn to the last page so we can see the signature there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, the page before. And could we also look at the B/C/S, please. Page 7. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And now could we look at e-court page 4 in the English and page 5 in the B/C/S, please, do you recall, in the interim, telling the truth to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sorry, it's the previous page. I'm interested in paragraph 17. And in the B/C/S the next -- no. We had the right page in the English. That's right. And in the B/C/S, can we turn the page, please. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let's look at paragraph 17. It reads: "After this investigation, the prisoners were returned to the detention room at the brigade. I knew that the prisoners remained there for a time as I used to walk down that passage on occasion. Some days later, I noticed that the prisoners were no longer there. I do not know what ... happened to the prisoners and have never received any official explanation as to what became of them. In my opinion, the brigade commander or the chief of security were the ones who made the decisions about the prisoners. I was not at any meetings where the fate of the prisoners were discussed." Now, sir, do you stand by what you -- your statement -- the -- what I've read out from your statement?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And yesterday you were asked whether you had any personal knowledge of what happened to these Muslim prisoners who you took statements from. And you said you didn't know, as I've just read out what had happened to them but you went on to tell this Chamber and this is at transcript 34299, starting at line 9: "I believe that they had joined the other prisoners of war and left, that they were driven away to Batkovic to a camp down there. I don't know what kind of camp that was in Bijeljina." Now, sir, the last known location of these prisoners was at the Standard Barracks, and these prisoners are still missing today. We have the record, and this Chamber has the record of the prisoners that were registered at the Batkovic collection centre and who were exchanged, and they are not amongst them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's P2132 for your reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: One of these four Muslim prisoners, Almir Halilovic, he was just around 15 years old, and he's still missing today. So I'm going to give you to opportunity to please tell us for the sake of his mother, his surviving relatives, what do you know about what happened to these prisoners and where can they be found?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already told you once that I did not make decisions and I have idea whatsoever who it was that did make decisions. I mean, what kind of question is this. I don't know. I mean, really, I don't know anything. As can you see from here I was just taking statements so that Nesko and his son would be punished. I'm sorry if this happened. I really have no idea what happened to them. Can somebody here believe what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time, and it would be a good time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we're even a bit late for the break. Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes after the break. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness to be escorted in the courtroom, it's not one of the best days of this Chamber. First of all, in relation to the guidance I gave in the margin this morning, well, whether it was guidance or not but I emphasised that for an update of a Rule 65 ter witness summary that you would have to seek approval. Now I think it's three years ago that we said that we allowed the parties to -- to do without that formality, so that is hereby corrected. Because at the time we said that the parties do not need to seek leave to amend the summaries which you would expect on the basis of the Rules but we desisted from that formality. Now, there's another matter, the verification of what the witness said yesterday about whether he remembered he had seen bruises and injuries on the faces of the prisoners. Turns out to be that there's a translation error and I will put that to the witness in a second when he enters the courtroom. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours had asked for us to report as to the video D917.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can report that we'll be submitting a compilation of the excerpts tomorrow on DVD.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is appreciated. Perhaps since we're still waiting for the witness, Ms. Hasan, you are again and again referring to having survived the massacre or the execution at Branjevo farm. Is it really survival or is it that they escaped it?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, they -- they escaped -- they survived and escaped it. I'm not sure I appreciate the distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem -- I had no opportunity to fully go back into the background of it, but if you are lost from a group before they end up at the location where there's an execution, then you could say you escape and therefore survive but in that respect, of course, many others -- those who escaped would not usually refer to as survivors.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So can I confirm that they survived. It's our position that they survived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then please forgive me that I do not have all the details of the evidence in my head, that's then clear. Witness, before we continue, I'd like to revisit a matter which we discussed earlier. When you said, I never told this Court that you had remembered that the -- that the imprisoned or the Muslims which were captured had bruises and injuries, we have that verified, and I think you rightly insisted on a verification. Because what was interpreted to us: "But I do remember that they had some bruises and injuries on their faces," should have been, the accurate translation should have been: "But I do remember that they did not have bruises and injuries on their faces and bodies," so it is hereby verified that you indeed denied to have seen bruises and injuries on their faces and bodies. I think in fairness to you, we should -- we should clarify this immediately. We have done so, and you were right. Please proceed, Ms. Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that the crime prevention unit which you were a member of was -- fell under the control of Drago Nikolic. I'd just like to understand the procedure that took place on a daily basis, and if you can confirm that I understand the procedure correctly. Namely, that on a daily basis, you would meet with the chief of security or inform him of the situation, as far as military detention is concerned, he would go to a briefing with the brigade commander, and after that, you and your colleagues would either be summoned by Drago Nikolic to his office or he would call you and he would hand down the instructions as to what your tasks were that day. Have I encapsulated that correctly?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, have you encapsulated the procedure correctly. But we are talking about the detention unit of the Zvornik Brigade and its combatants; you didn't say that. We informed him how many men were in detention from the Zvornik Brigade and as far as the Muslim prisoners are concerned, let me explain about the detention of the Zvornik Brigade. We kept full records. We knew how much detention was ordered by the battalion commander up to 15 days and so on and so forth. As for Muslim prisoners, our service did not from any information, we didn't know their number, we did not keep their records, nor did anybody ever inform us about any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you slow down, please, because otherwise the interpreters are unable to follow you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If necessary, I will repeat. Shall I repeat? Shall I explain again? What you said about our meetings with Drago Nikolic is correct but those meetings were exclusively linked to the Zvornik Brigade detention, i.e., the detention of the Zvornik Brigade where the combatants of the Zvornik Brigade were kept.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Witness, I'll just stop you because we do have your complete answer, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were at risk to speak in your correction as fast as you did the first time. So could you please slow down in your following answers. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So when Drago Nikolic was absent, who would have been the person who provided you with instructions?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His deputy, Milorad Trbic. But I repeat. That applied only to the combatants of the Zvornik Brigade who were detained.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And as far as any combat-related tasks were concerned within the sphere of the military police, who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the military police company, Lieutenant Miomir Jasikovac. However, the crime prevention department did not get engaged in combat. The police themselves very seldom were. We were involved in policing duties, bringing people in, controlling bridges, traffic control. There were three military police platoons within the military police company and there was also our department, the crime prevention department. We were never engaged in combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, the Standard Barracks we've been talking about, where were they located?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the main road between Zvornik and Bijeljina, say, about 3 kilometres away from town.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And your reference to Zvornik, I understand, would be the town of Zvornik; is that correct? So it fell between the town of Zvornik and Bijeljina in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: The barracks themselves, they comprised of two floors; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's a ground floor and there is a floor upstairs, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And on the floor upstairs were the offices of Pandurevic, Obrenovic, Drago Nikolic, and the operations duty room. Do I have that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your office, you've told us, was on the ground floor. Where was the infirmary?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And am I right that you actually slept at the barracks in the dormitory during that time-period?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you would have passed the infirmary on a daily basis to go to the dormitory.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, do you recall during the time -- during that time-period, and I know you're not very good with dates, but before 23 July between 10 to 15 wounded Muslim prisoners were brought to the infirmary at the Standard Barracks at the Zvornik hospital. Now, they were under the care of the chief of the medical centre of the Zvornik Brigade, Dr. Zoran Begovic, and they were receiving treatment. Do you recall these patients? One of them had an amputated lower leg.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember if somebody had an amputated leg, but I think that I saw wounded Muslim prisoners as I passed by, by the infirmary. It's a hall that I have to go through in order to go upstairs to sleep there. As for this amputated leg, I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now, Dr. Zoran Begovic has testified before this Tribunal in the Popovic case, and he said that these wounded prisoners were secured by military policemen. You saw military policemen standing guard?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember the details now. Possibly. Possibly. I really do not remember who it was that guarded them.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: These prisoners you saw -- these wounded prisoners you saw them being put on a truck, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truck was at the other entrance into the Standard Barracks there was the main entrance where the entrance to the command was and there was this other entrance and that's where they -- I've already talked about this. Two trucks stopped and, I mean, well, they were put onto the truck. Now whether it was these wounded persons, I've already said, according to my estimate, and I can see that from my office when I was sitting up there, perhaps it's about 50 metres away, I saw Muslim prisoners being put onto the truck, and they were driven away somewhere. I asked later on, but I was unofficially told that they were being taken to Batkovic. But then I've already talked about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Okay. These trucks, were there VRS soldiers around them?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't know them. I don't think they were from the Zvornik Brigade, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Were they military policemen?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now, I cannot recall. They were people in uniform but whether they were military policemen, I really cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Did you see Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic from the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic? I don't know him. I think I've never seen him. Maybe I did see him actually but I didn't know who it was. So I really don't know who this man is. I heard of Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, I heard that he was in the corps. But, personally I never saw him. I mean, I never met him. We were never introduced. Maybe I came across him, but I did not know that it was Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Now you say you heard of a Lieutenant Popovic. You didn't know who Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic, chief of the security of the Drina Corps, was from your superior command?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I never met Popovic, I never sat with him, but I did hear that Popovic is the chief of security of the Drina Corps. I state that with certainty. But I don't know what the man looks like at all. That is certainly correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So in relation to what you just testified and specifically you said that you didn't know -- couldn't remember whether -- now, whether it was these wounded persons who were put on the truck. Let's see if can I help you remember. Now, you recall that you testified, as I've shown you before the transcript of your testimony in Trbic case in 2007 before the State Court.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If we can call that up again. It's 65 ter 32420. Could we see page 23.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And again, this is only in English, Mr. Jeremic, so I'll read it slowly so that can you follow along.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Can we direct -- can we look down to line 23, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Question was put to you: "Have you ever been informed, did you ever find out when these Bosniak prisoners, the injured ones, left the barracks? " "A. Well, I wasn't informed as to when they were brought there or when they were taken away, but actually I saw when - how to put it? - I saw them boarding a truck that was at another entrance. They were placed there, and rumours had it that they were taken to Batkovici for an exchange. But I didn't see them leaving the compound, I didn't see them whether they went to the left or to the right of the barracks. "Q. When you saw them getting on the truck, were there any VRS soldiers around? "A. Yes. "Q. From which unit were they from? "A. I believe that they were unknown soldiers, but I can't claim that with certainty ..." Do you stand by that testimony you gave to the State Court.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't know which unit. I didn't know where they went, and what I said, that they were taken to Batkovic, that is what people were saying in the barracks. A soldier could have walked by and I said, Where are these people going? And he said, To Batkovic. Somebody sort of heard that they were going to Batkovic but I don't see why I would be receiving information as to where Muslim prisoners were being taken. I really don't know. I was just an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: There's evidence in this case that on the morning of the 23rd of July, Vinko Pandurevic asked for a solution, that a solution be found for the wounded prisoners because there was a problem with sending them back to Zvornik hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's P2139, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And he's told shortly after that that Popovic will arrive at 1700 hours to say what needs to be done regarding the "work" that was talked about. And this, Your Honours, can be found in P2140, and the Zvornik Brigade duty officer notebook for 23 July. Now, there's evidence that around the 23rd of July, military policemen took the wounded prisoners from the infirmary and they were executed. Now, surely these wounded prisoners, there was a lot of talk at these barracks, surely you knew that these men were taken away to be executed?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary, there was no talk, and I never heard about this. This is the first time I'm hearing of this, from you. Not where they were taken, not who took them. You've told me just now. It's the first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm going to move on now to the buses you spoke about yesterday that you saw transporting male prisoners under the guard of members of the VRS. This is at transcript page 34280, starting at line 3. Can you describe what you were able to observe about the men on those buses?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already testified about that. I can repeat. I will repeat that this Standard Barracks, the barracks of the Zvornik Brigade buses passed by it and there were guards inside and --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I just want you to specifically focus on the men that you saw inside the buses. Now, what did you observe about them? How were they seated? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buses passed by quickly, and I could notice that men were sitting in the seats and that they were looking into the ground and that they held their hands above their heads and that in the buses there were uniformed Serb soldiers who were standing there, and the bus was going from Zvornik to Bijeljina, that is what I saw for sure and that is what I already stated.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And when you say their hands were above their heads, do you mean to say that their hands were sort of raised up high or were they clasped behind their necks?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their hands were clasped behind their necks and their heads were bend down, and uniformed Serb soldiers were standing next to them and then the bus passed by, didn't stop in front of the barracks so I didn't see who the soldiers were, and you couldn't really recognise anyone at that moment, what unit they came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to the day that you were on guard duty at the gate of the Standard Barracks. There were no MPs at the barracks at that time; correct? Sorry, is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they went out into the field, and I was told by the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear who.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- stay at the gate. I don't know where they went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who told you that, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander of the company of the military police, Lieutenant Jasikovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And it was precisely because there was nobody left at the barracks that Commander Jasikovac assigned you to gate duty; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Jasikovac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You -- it wasn't part of your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that an answer to the question, I wonder? Did Commander Jasikovac assigned you to gate duty because there was nobody left at the barracks? Was that the situation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all military policemen, how do I put this? They got ready and went somewhere in the field and he said to me, Jeremic, you're going to stay at the gate on guard duty and I stayed at the gate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your colleagues, Goran Bogdanovic and Cedo Jovic, they weren't assigned to the gate. They went to the field; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we take a look at P1565. And, Your Honours, and the Defence, I have the original here. I think the Defence has seen this attendance roster of the military police before. We've shown it on -- it was displayed on the screen yesterday, but I think for the purposes of the next questions it would be beneficial to have the original before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And on the screens could we see page 3, and I think it suffices, since we're seen this before, to just have the original B/C/S displayed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: If you could look -- you see where your name is. You're listed number 6. Number 5 is Goran Bogdanovic. Number 7 is Cedo Jovic. And if you can just move your eyes along the columns and take a look at the column numbered 14. So this is the 14th of July. You see there's a plus sign for your name and there is what appears to be on the face of the document a T, which is an indication of in the field, for Goran Bogdanovic and Cedo Jovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And if you look to the right and left of that, we see indication that Goran Bogdanovic and Cedo Jovic are present at the barracks. So, sir, the day you were standing guard at the gate when Cedo Jovic and Goran Bogdanovic were in the field was the 14th of July; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the reason I put that document in front of you is to -- and I think -- I believe we have shown you this before, is to look at some underlying markings beneath the markings of T that are ... marked under the Ts for Goran Bogdanovic and Cedo Jovic. We can even blow up the one that is on the screen. Just for the column closer to the -- to the -- if we can blow up 13, 14, 15, 16 July, that area. So it's somewhat visible there on the screen, and it should be even better in the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sir, when your colleagues Bogdanovic and Jovic returned from the field, what did they tell you about where they were?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't tell me anything. Nobody really said much at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: They told you that they were in Orahovac, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter 32395. And, Your Honours, I'll just ask that you keep the original just momentarily with you. 65 ter 32395.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Sir, you remember testifying in the Popovic case, and you testified in 2007 and then again in 2008 for the Defence. So first as a Prosecution witness, and then as a Defence witness. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And you told the truth to that Trial Chamber, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Could we have a look at e-court page 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Lines 21 is where I'm going to begin reading, and I'm reading this out to you because it's in English. "Q. So when you testified a couple of moments ago that 'some of them told me where they were in the field,' can you just tell the Trial Chamber who told you and what did they tell you about where they were in the field? Then I'll move on. "A. Well, my work-mates, Bogdanovic and some others, told me they were in Orahovac, in the field there. I know about them. I didn't ask anyone else about anything of the sort." Do you stand by that testimony you gave to the Popovic Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I said that then, then it's correct. It's correct probably. He possibly told me -- it was a long time ago. 20 years ago. I really can't remember every single detail. It is possible. Very well. Yes, okay. He told me. Let's stick to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: In fact, sir, not only did --

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. But he did not tell me one or two days later. I suppose he told me perhaps even seven days later. I really can't give you any dates. Yes. I can't give you anything in terms of time reference, whether it was three, five or seven days later or a month later, but it was a long time ago. But, okay, I accept that he did tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, in fact, you were told that the Muslim prisoners were being shot at Orahovac. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But he -- that he did not shoot at them. That he threw his rifle and that he refused to shoot at them. That's what he told me and I still claim that to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: So you confirm that you were told that there were executions taking place in Orahovac where your colleagues were present.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I know that you're not. And as to when he told me that, I don't know. He -- he may have told me. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question simply is whether he told you that or not. That's the -- that's what --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Ms. Hasan is asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I know but the question was when he told me that. I can't tell you. I can't remember when he told me maybe he told me three months thereafter or perhaps six months later. I really don't know. Maybe he told me that once the war was over. I can't remember when he said that. And this is my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But the question doesn't ask you when you were being told, sir. You were just asked whether you were told.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And, in fact, he told you, as you just testified a few minutes ago, that he refused to shoot at these people, he threw his gun away; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what he told me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: You had also heard from Zvornik Brigade soldiers in the days after you saw the buses pass by the Standard Barracks carrying, transporting Muslim men, that executions were also taking place in Pilica; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that? I don't understand your question. Are you saying that I said that? Did I state that? Or are you putting a question to me?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Well, I'll -- I'm first putting the question to you, which is that you had heard from soldiers that executions were taking place in Pilica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was "heard from Zvornik Brigade soldiers."

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, not much was said about that. People kept quiet about that. Not much was said at all. Whether I heard something or not - and if I did, when I heard what I did - I really don't know how to answer your question. Indeed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Let me see if I can help a little bit.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go on. Give it your best shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: 65 ter 32393, please, e-court page 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Again, this is your testimony in the Popovic case. See, I'm going to read, starting at line 6. Sorry, if we can just scroll up, I'll read the question so that's clear: "Q. At some time after this day when you saw those buses, did you begin to hear rumours at the brigade? And if so, can you tell the Trial Chamber what those rumours were that you heard? "A. After that, I don't know exactly how many days later, I can't give you a date as to when, but I heard that there were executions of Muslims in Orahovac and Pilica. Those were the rumours that were going round in the brigades or, rather, at Standard I heard this from the soldiers. No one said anything officially, but many of them were talking about it." Do you stand by that testimony you gave?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by what I said then. I suppose that there were rumours. But I don't know when. Yes, there were rumours. Probably there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Were you or - to your knowledge - anyone in your unit instructed to conduct any investigations into these executions that took place at Orahovac and Pilica?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever asked for that officially. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And, sir, just to clarify, you say "not officially." Were you unofficially asked to conduct any investigations?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody ever requested that. None of the officers ever told me about that. Whatever I'm telling you is based on hearsay, on what the soldiers were talking about, what I heard on the street, what rumours I heard. Nobody ever shared that information with me in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions. Only to say that it's the Prosecution's position that the document that is before you, the attendance roster, under the T markings for Goran Bogdanovic and Cedo Jovic, are the letters O, and there's testimony on that as well in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you remind us what the letter O stands for on the legend.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Orahovac, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that in the legend or is that your interpretation? Because we see TO as in the terrain, but not Orahovac. The O then stands for a different location.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: It is in the legend, Your Honour. We can turn to it, P1565, and -- yes. In fact, it's -- this document is a document that we've raised before, and that there were certain erasures made to it. One of the erasures made was for the defined term -- for the definition of the term O, and if you look at the last --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: -- few pages. And it is probably, in fact, more visible in the original before you but we'll have to zoom in, I don't know how good this scan is, it's difficult for me to see on the scan. I can definitely see it on the original, Your Honours. We do also have an expert report that was of an examination of this document which is not in evidence in this case. But it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But we are looking at this moment at the legend in English which seems not to correspond with the legend in B/C/S or am I wrong? SL or C means off and then this is the one which corresponds with what we... yes. And there it says TO stands for in the field and osnaci.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I believe it's -- if you look at the original, it should be ... I can't properly see it on this scan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently we have two different pages with legenda because we looked at -- that we look at another one before? Yes. At least in English translation of.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yeah. But the erasure that I'm referring to, it should be, if you look at the original, where the T is. It is Teren and I'm not sure it's helpful to look at the screen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's say the following. I have a -- although a bit of it, a vague recollection that we looked at it in quite some detail in the past. Let's re-read that rather than to now, where there's no need to do it with the witness, to try to reconstruct any matters which we should take more time for.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And I will provide those references for you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we leave this page here, Madam Hasan, I don't see any symbol that stands as an O alone on this legend.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: That's correct. Because it's our position that the legend included an O with a definition Orahovac, which was erased over which T and Teren was replaced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the entries was [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I think that is explained in the testimony which I will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And Orahovac was deleted from the legend.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the Prosecution's position, let's be clear about that. We don't have to verify it with the witness now.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: And Your Honour, it is visible. The erasure is visible in the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Not the pages you have provided to us at this moment, but we received four -- or perhaps it's at the back. Unfortunately, I have forgotten my glasses today, but Judge Moloto.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: I'd be much worse without my glasses, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Somebody attend to Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's very helpful of you, Mr. Mladic. I have -- I have an opportunity to later look at it again with my glasses and I don't know whether your glasses and my glasses present the same picture. That is still to be seen. Well, nothing is translated, but I take it that this is a friendly gesture which is addressed to me. No need to communicate that with the public gallery.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll return it to you. I think that you're referring to, where there seems to be an empty line in the legenda that there was something there before. That's how we have to understand it, if we would follow your view.

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: Yes. It should be around exactly where you've pointed out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, between "teren" and "teren Zepa." No further questions? Or do you have any --

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. That would be all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you would just give me one second, please. I'm just re-reading a portion of the evidence which may cause me to ask questions, but I'm not certain about it yet. Any further questions, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Jeremic, do you remember the date when you were actually on duty at the gate? Do you remember that date at all?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see that it was on the 13th or the 14th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's be very clear. Is that your recollection or is that what you conclude on the basis of the documents that have been put before you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm basing that on the documents that have been put before me. When all the MPs went on a field mission, I knew that it was sometime around the 11th or the 12 or the 13th but I wasn't sure. Now I can see that that was the day or the time when I was on the gate duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And let me finish with the following question. Today when you've just seen this document, do you still stand by the claim that was 24 hours before the passage of the buses and lorries about which you were asked?

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I stand by that statement. That was 24 hours prior to the time when I saw that the buses were passing by the Standard Barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremic, thank you on behalf of the Mladic Defence. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: NEBOJSA JEREMIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Any further questions, Ms. Hasan?

utterances.speaker: MS. HASAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jeremic, this concludes your testimony in this Court. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague. It's quite a journey. And I wanted to thank you for having answered all the questions that were put to you, put to you by the parties, put to you by the Judges. I wish you a safe return home again. You may now follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did my best to answer all the questions. Thank you for the good wishes. And I wish you a pleasant day, and I bid you all farewell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was the last witness for this week, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I have a few matters still on my agenda. We could do two things. We can deal -- try to deal with them before we adjourn or take a break now and deal with them after a break and adjourn after I've dealt with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, wish -- we suggest that we should continue and adjourn before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll deal with a few procedural matters but give me just one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is -- the first item concerns D918. On the 26th of February of this year, D918 was marked for identification pending a translation. Is the Defence in a position to give an update on the translation? It's about Goran Krcmar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, our colleague Lukic did that. We will check, and we will inform you within the shortest possible time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Preferably not later than the 15th of April and, of course, that cannot be done then in court but perhaps an update through e-mail would already serve the purpose. The second one is also dealing with the remaining issue from the testimony of Goran Krcmar and is about P7172 which was marked for identification on the 3rd of March, 2015 pending a translation. On 17th of March the Prosecution e-mailed the Chamber and the Defence, advising that the translation has been uploaded into e-court under doc ID ZA-01-7670-BCST. And the Chamber wonders whether the Defence has any objections. Another way of dealing with it is that we would admit and that the Defence has an opportunity to revisit the matter. And perhaps we should give in view of the present circumstances a bit more time than usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be fair. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7172 is admitted into evidence and you have one week to revisit the matter. Then there's another remaining issue from the testimony of Milos Solaja, P7 ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the extent I have been unclear in relation to that, the uploaded translation which I just mentioned for P7172 can be attached and the Registrar is instructed to do so, to MFI P7172.
