Then I move onto P7196, remaining issue from the testimony of Milos Solaja. On the 9th of March, P7196, which is a transcript from the 22nd Session of the Republika Srpska Assembly, dated 23rd and 24th of November, 1992, was marked for identification pending an agreement between the parties as to which excerpt of the transcript should be tendered. This is to be found at transcript pages 32795 through -96. On the 7th of April, the Prosecution advised the Chamber via an e-mail that it uploaded into e-court under 65 ter number 02362a, the introduction and the portion of the transcript that was used with the witness. Is there any objection from the Defence to the admission of this document as -- in its present format?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, according to my information, we have no objection. But, again I would suggest that you give us this time but do admit it like the previous document. I'm saying this out of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Registry is hereby instructed to attach 65 ter 02362a to P7196. P7196 is admitted into evidence and the Defence has an opportunity within one week to revisit the matter in terms of objections. The following item deals with P6996 and is a remaining issue from the testimony of Vojo Kupresanin. On the 11th of December of last year, P6996, which is an intercepted telephone conversation between Jovo Tintor and Mirko Jovic, was marked for identification pending the formation by the Defence of its objection. I refer to transcript pages 29692 to -694. On the 26th of March, the Chamber set a deadline of the 30th of March for the Defence to make submissions. On the 30th of March, Mr. Ivetic e-mailed the Chamber advising that: "Mr. Lukic will be in a better position to provide an explanation of that objection tomorrow, in so far as he is the attorney that dealt with the witness and made the objection in question." However, as of today, Mr. Lukic has not made any submissions. The question therefore arises whether the objection to P6996 can be articulated now or not. I think that we'll follow the same road as we did before, that is, where Mr. Lukic has not articulated the objection any further, that P6996 is admitted into evidence but if Mr. Lukic wants to revisit the matter, he has an opportunity to do so, and since we're not in Court next week, he should do it in writing. He can do so within one week from now. I move on to my next item which is a remaining issue from, again, the testimony of Goran Krcmar. It's D920. On the 2nd of March of this year, D920 was marked for identification pending a translation. On the 10th of March, the Defence advised the Chamber via an e-mail that the translation had been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 1D19-1412. On the 30th of March, the Prosecution indicated that it had no objection to the translation per se but it was unable to identify the point during Witness Krcmar's testimony when D920 was actually discussed. This can be found at transcript page 33849. The Prosecution made further submissions in this regard on the 31st of March which can be found at transcript pages 33891 through -92. In summary, the Prosecution had doubts that the document was used during the course of Witness Krcmar's testimony. And the question of the Chamber is whether the Defence has had an opportunity to verify the transcripts in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that was again Mr. Lukic, but my recollection was that he and Mr. Traldi had spoken and had agreed that one particular document had not been previously used, if this is the one that is at issue. But either Mr. Traldi or Mr. Lukic would be the ones to give more detailed information. I was only a by-stander to their conversation about this in the courtroom the other week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, could the parties inform the Chamber not later than by next week. Meanwhile, the Registry is instructed to attach doc ID 1D19-1412 to D920 but no decision on admission is yet there. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, who was apparently following the proceedings remotely, confirms that Mr. Ivetic's recollection is correct and so the discussion that Mr. Ivetic was just referring to between Mr. Lukic and Mr. Traldi referred to the document the Court was addressing a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the issue apparently being whether or not the document was actually discussed during the testimony, I leave it to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's what the discussion -- between Mr. Lukic and Mr. Traldi was about and Mr. Lukic acknowledged that he had not used the document. And, therefore, it presumable would be withdrawn as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's -- the last line you spoke is the matter I would speak clarification by the Defence, whether they withdraw tendering it, or whether they think that it should be admitted by other means than through this witness. That's the question I left open. And we'd like to hear from the Defence also within the next week what their plans are in relation to D920. Then I have one final matter. On the 7th of April, the Defence has e-mailed the Chamber requesting leave to add 65 ter 1D05382 to the 65 ter exhibit list for Witness Nebojsa Jeremic. My agenda reads whether the Prosecution has any objections. But since apparently this document was not introduced through this witnesses, and, therefore, the point in time where we usually deal with additions to the 65 ter list, that is, if it comes to the tendering of it, it seems that the matter is moot because, unless for other reasons you would still like to have it on the 65 ter exhibit list, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's not a clear answer to my question. Is the matter moot? Or would you, for other reasons, still want to have it on your 65 ter exhibit list?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need to keep it on the 65 ter list, so it can be deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This request is declared moot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may refer back to D920, if this will help the parties, what was admitted as D920 but marked for identification was 65 er 1D5367. If that helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sure it helps someone on our team; unfortunately not the personnel that are here today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the parties could verify whether, because my colleague Judge Moloto has made an annotation with that number during the hearing so it must have been referred to in one way or another. But whether it was tendered or used specifically or with the witness, can you please verify that so the Chamber will finally have full information how to deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
